nrl.title: NRL Plasma Formulary: D-T reactivity tables
nrl.note: The <σv> polynomial is fit through six NRL table points (1–50 keV). Slightly simplified for gameplay: true Bosch-Hale parameterization uses a rational function with NRL-tabulated coefficients.

ipb98.title: ITER Physics Basis, Chapter 2: confinement scaling IPB98(y,2)
ipb98.note: Game uses τ_E ∝ H·B^0.15·P^-0.69·n^0.41 with machine size folded into one calibration constant. The full law also scales with plasma current I_p^0.93, major radius R^1.97, elongation, and isotope mass.

lawson.title: Lawson criterion. Power balance in a burning plasma
lawson.source: J.D. Lawson, Proc. Phys. Soc. B 70, 6 (1957)
lawson.note: Ignition threshold n·T·τ_E ≥ 3×10²¹ keV·s·m⁻³ for D-T at optimum temperature.

greenwald.title: Density limits in toroidal plasmas
greenwald.source: M. Greenwald, Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 44, R27 (2002)
greenwald.note: Empirical limit n_GW = I_p/(πa²) in 10²⁰ m⁻³. Exceeding it triggers edge radiative collapse and disruption. Game maps plasma current to the toroidal field setting.

troyon.title: MHD-limit to plasma confinement (Troyon beta limit)
troyon.source: F. Troyon et al., Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 26, 209 (1984)
troyon.note: Normalized beta limit β_N ≈ 2.8. Game uses a fixed β limit of 2.8% for simplicity.

jet_record.title: JET D-T record campaign: 16.1 MW fusion power, Q ≈ 0.67
jet_record.source: M. Keilhacker et al., Nuclear Fusion 39, 209 (1999)
jet_record.note: The 1997 world record that stood for a generation; JET's 2021 campaign later set the total-energy record of 59 MJ.

divertor_iter.title: ITER divertor design: tungsten monoblock targets, ~10-20 MW/m² steady state
divertor_iter.source: R.A. Pitts et al., Nuclear Materials and Energy 20, 100696 (2019)
divertor_iter.note: Tungsten recrystallizes around 1200-1300 °C; actively-cooled monoblocks push tolerable surface temperatures toward 2000 °C transiently.

dpa_materials.title: Neutron-induced displacement damage in first-wall materials
dpa_materials.source: S.J. Zinkle & G.S. Was, Acta Materialia 61, 735 (2013)
dpa_materials.note: A commercial plant's first wall accumulates tens of dpa per full-power year. Game compresses this to a 120-minute depletion at 500 MW for playability.

quench.title: Superconducting magnet quench: stored-energy dump dynamics
quench.source: ITER magnet system technical basis / L. Bottura, CERN Yellow Reports
quench.note: ITER's toroidal field coils store 41 GJ. A quench converts superconductor to resistive metal in milliseconds; the energy must go somewhere.

rebco_arc.title: ARC: a compact high-field reactor enabled by REBCO superconductors
rebco_arc.source: B.N. Sorbom et al., Fusion Eng. Des. 100, 378 (2015)
rebco_arc.note: REBCO tape allows ~20 T on-coil fields. Fusion power density scales roughly as B⁴. The entire premise of compact commercial fusion (and of SPARC/CFS).

tbr.title: Tritium breeding blankets and fuel self-sufficiency
tbr.source: M. Abdou et al., Nuclear Fusion 61, 013001 (2021)
tbr.note: A power reactor must breed its own tritium from ⁶Li(n,α)T with TBR slightly above 1. No operating reactor has yet demonstrated this at scale.

tritium_price.title: Tritium supply: CANDU byproduct, ~$30,000/gram, kg-scale world inventory
tritium_price.source: Abdou et al. (2021); DOE Fusion Energy Sciences supply assessments
tritium_price.note: World civilian tritium inventory is only ~25 kg. A 500 MW D-T plant burns ~28 kg/year. Market fuel is economically impossible; breeding is mandatory.

recirc.title: Recirculating power and net electric output in fusion plant designs
recirc.source: ARIES Advanced Tokamak Power Plant Studies, UC San Diego
recirc.note: Heating systems, cryogenics, and pumping can consume 20-30% of gross electric output. Q_engineering, not Q_plasma, decides commercial viability.

lcoe_lazard.title: Lazard's Levelized Cost of Energy Analysis (v16)
lcoe_lazard.note: Utility-scale solar/wind: $24-96/MWh; gas combined cycle: $39-101/MWh. Fusion must land inside this band to matter commercially.

thermal_eff.title: Balance-of-plant thermal conversion efficiency (~35% Rankine baseline)
thermal_eff.source: ARIES systems studies; conventional steam-cycle engineering
thermal_eff.note: Advanced Brayton cycles project 45%+, but 35% is the conservative baseline for a first-of-a-kind plant.

iter_physics.title: ITER Physics Basis (full volume)
iter_physics.source: Nuclear Fusion 39, issue 12 (1999) and Progress in ITER Physics Basis, NF 47 (2007)
iter_physics.note: The consensus physics reference underpinning burning-plasma tokamak design.

doe_fusion.title: DOE Office of Science: Fusion Energy Sciences
doe_fusion.note: Fuel energy density comparison: fusion fuel yields ~10 million times the energy of an equal mass of coal.

nbi.title: Neutral beam injection heating: deposition and shine-through
nbi.source: E. Speth, Reports on Progress in Physics 52, 57 (1989)
nbi.note: Beam ions deposit via collisions, so absorption falls with plasma density; at low density a large fraction shines through to the far wall. Real NBI systems interlock on shine-through power to protect the vessel.

hmode.title: Regime of improved confinement (H-mode) discovered on ASDEX
hmode.source: F. Wagner et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 49, 1408 (1982)
hmode.note: The spontaneous edge transport barrier that roughly doubles confinement. The operating regime of every modern tokamak design.

stellarator_w7x.title: Wendelstein 7-X: optimized stellarator confinement without plasma current
stellarator_w7x.source: T. Klinger et al., Nuclear Fusion 59, 112004 (2019)
stellarator_w7x.note: Stellarators need no driven current, eliminating current-driven disruptions. At the cost of fearsome coil complexity and maintenance.

scram.title: Disruption mitigation and machine protection in tokamaks
scram.source: E.M. Hollmann et al., Physics of Plasmas 22, 021802 (2015)
scram.note: Real machines fire shattered-pellet injectors to radiate plasma energy before it hits the wall. Historical disruptions at JET and TFTR informed the failure modes in this game.

point_kinetics.title: Point reactor kinetics with delayed neutrons
point_kinetics.source: J.R. Lamarsh, Introduction to Nuclear Reactor Theory (1966), ch. 7
point_kinetics.note: Delayed neutrons (β ≈ 0.65% for U-235) are why reactors are controllable at all. Game uses the prompt-jump approximation of the kinetics equations.

prompt_crit.title: Prompt criticality and the Chernobyl excursion
prompt_crit.note: When reactivity exceeds the delayed-neutron fraction, power multiplies on prompt neutrons alone. Microseconds, not seconds. No control system can follow it.

doppler.title: Doppler fuel-temperature coefficient
doppler.source: NRC Reactor Concepts Manual; Lamarsh ch. 7
doppler.note: Hot U-238 absorbs more neutrons (broadened resonances), automatically damping power rises. The key inherent safety feature of light-water reactors.

xenon.title: Xenon-135 poisoning and the iodine pit
xenon.source: Lamarsh ch. 11; WNA physics of reactor kinetics
xenon.note: Xe-135 has a huge neutron appetite. After a power drop it builds from iodine decay for ~9 hours and can make restart impossible. A factor in the Chernobyl test setup.

decay_heat.title: Decay heat and the Three Mile Island accident
decay_heat.source: NRC: The TMI-2 Accident (NUREG-0600); ANS decay-heat standard
decay_heat.note: Fission products keep releasing ~6-7% of full power immediately after shutdown. TMI-2 melted hours after its reactor had already tripped. Cooling must continue.

pwr.title: Pressurized water reactor systems
pwr.note: Game models a ~3400 MWth PWR: two-node thermal hydraulics, ~33% steam-cycle efficiency, and steam generators fatigued by thermal cycling.

asme.title: ASME Boiler & Pressure Vessel Code, Section III. Nuclear components
asme.note: Sets allowable stress intensities (Sm) and the fatigue design rules (cumulative usage factor via Miner's rule) every nuclear pressure part is licensed against.

pts.title: Pressurized thermal shock and vessel embrittlement screening
pts.note: Fast-neutron fluence shifts the vessel steel's ductile-to-brittle transition (RT_NDT). Exceed the screening limit and the vessel can no longer be shown safe against cold-water shock.

dnbr.title: Departure from nucleate boiling ratio (W-3 correlation)
dnbr.source: L.S. Tong, Boiling Crisis and Critical Heat Flux (1972)
dnbr.note: If the heat flux exceeds the critical value, a vapor film blankets the fuel and clad temperature jumps hundreds of degrees. Plants keep DNBR above ~1.3 with 95/95 confidence.

ecc.title: Emergency core cooling acceptance criteria
ecc.note: Peak cladding temperature must stay below 2200 °F (1204 °C) in design-basis accidents. Above that, zirconium cladding oxidizes runaway-fast in steam.

case_chernobyl.title: INSAG-7: The Chernobyl Accident, Updating of INSAG-1
case_chernobyl.note: The definitive post-Soviet analysis: reactor design flaws (positive void coefficient, positive scram effect) combined with operation outside the permitted regime.

case_tmi.title: Report of the President's Commission on the Accident at Three Mile Island (Kemeny Commission)
case_tmi.source: U.S. Government Printing Office (1979); NRC backgrounder
case_tmi.note: A stuck-open relief valve, misleading instrumentation, and operators trained to fear a full pressurizer let decay heat destroy half the core.

case_fukushima.title: The Fukushima Daiichi Accident: Report by the Director General
case_fukushima.note: The reactors survived the earthquake and scrammed correctly. The tsunami drowned the diesel generators, and without power for cooling, decay heat did the rest.

case_sl1.title: SL-1 accident investigation (U.S. AEC, 1961-1962)
case_sl1.source: U.S. Atomic Energy Commission / General Electric final report (IDO series)
case_sl1.note: Overview with the primary AEC reports in its references. A single manually-withdrawn control rod took a small core prompt critical in about 4 milliseconds.

case_windscale.title: The Windscale fire of October 1957 (Penney inquiry)
case_windscale.note: Overview with the declassified inquiry in its references. Stored Wigner energy in the graphite, released during an annealing run with sparse instrumentation, set the uranium cartridges alight.

case_tokaimura.title: Report on the preliminary fact-finding mission following the accident at the nuclear fuel processing facility in Tokaimura, Japan
case_tokaimura.note: Workers mixed enriched uranium solution in a wide precipitation tank by bucket, bypassing geometry controls. The solution went critical in the tank.
